correctness.rationale: Independently recover the restricted scalar identity as follows. For a unit f, D_f^p is a derivation commuting with D_f; its coefficient divided by f therefore has zero derivative and is constant. Write rho=[x^(p-1)](1/f). The normalized coordinate y with derivative f_0(1/f-rho*x^(p-1)) is defined by integration in degrees 0 through p-2 and has y=x+O(x^2). In this coordinate the coefficient of D is A+B*y^(p-1) with A=f_0, B=-f_0^2*rho. Applying D^p to y and taking constants gives B*(p-1)!*A^(p-1): each of the p-1 remaining applications must lower by one. Dividing by A gives lambda=f_0^p*rho=[x^(p-1)]f^(p-1). The unit operator is cyclic by the distinct descending leading degrees of the iterates of x^(p-1); lambda varies bijectively with f_(p-1) for each fixed lower tuple. For f_0=0, f_1 nonzero, triangularity gives distinct eigenvalues i*f_1, with p-1 choices of f_1 precisely for nonzero (p-1)-st powers. If f starts in degree k>=2, the h-th power raises the first degree of x^j by h(k-1), with nonzero leading coefficient exactly when j+h(k-1)<p. Its power ranks are max(p-1-h(k-1),0), giving the claimed lengths and the constant block. The strata sum correctly, including the zero tuple. On the nonzero roots Frobenius multiplies by lambda^((q-1)/(p-1)); this identifies the quotient by (p-1)-st powers with the roots of unity and yields orbits of length d and the stated M_d. These are natural-action multiplicities, not adjoint invariants.
residual_risks: The stored finite tests do not certify the Frobenius classification independently; that conclusion follows from the symbolic orbit argument.
